## Introduction

This project uses the Bank Marketing dataset to predict whether a customer subscribes to a term deposit after being contacted during a marketing campaign by a Portuguese banking institution. The response variable, `y`, records subscription status (`yes` or `no`). Customer demographics, financial information, and marketing contact characteristics provide possible predictors. 

The data were used in ST 558 Project 2 and originate from the [Kaggle Banking Dataset (Marketing Targets)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/prakharrathi25/banking-dataset-marketing-targets), based on the [UCI Bank Marketing dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/222/bank+marketing). The original training and testing files from Kaggle were combined and duplicate rows removed in Project 2. **A new training/test split will be created for this final project**; the original Kaggle split is not used for model evaluation.

Our goal is to compare a classification tree and a random forest using the `tidymodels` framework, select the better-performing model on a held-out test set, and make predictions available through an API.

## Data Loading & Preprocessing

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Read the cleaned dataset created for Project 2
bank_data <- read_csv("Dataset/bank_clean.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Convert categorical columns (including the response) to facotrs)
categorical_vars <- c(
  "job", "marital", "education", "default", "housing", "loan",
  "contact", "month", "poutcome", "y"
)

bank_data <- bank_data |>
  mutate(across(all_of(categorical_vars), as.factor))

# Put `yes` first so later classification metrics can treat it as the event
bank_data <- bank_data |>
  mutate(y = factor(y, levels = c("yes", "no")))
```

The cleaned dataset contains `r nrow(bank_data)` observations and `r ncol(bank_data)` variables. Numeric variables include customer age, account balance, and campaign contact measures; categorical variables include job, education, housing loan status, and the response.

### Dataset dimensions and variable types

```{r}
#| label: variable-types

tibble(
  Variable = names(bank_data),
  Type = vapply(bank_data, function(x) class(x)[1], character(1))
) |>
  kable(caption = "Variables and their data types")
```

### Missing values and duplicates

```{r}
#| label: data-quality

missing_summary <- tibble(
  Variable = names(bank_data),
  Missing = vapply(bank_data, function(x) sum(is.na(x)), integer(1))
)

missing_summary |>
  kable(caption = "Missing values by variable")

sum(duplicated(bank_data))
```

The value `unknown` appears in some categorical variables and is retained as a category rather than automatically treated as missing. The duplicate count above verifies whether any identical records remain in the cleaned dataset.

## Exploratory Analaysis of the Response

### Term deposit subscription frequencies

```{r}
#| label: response-distribution

subscription_summary <- bank_data |>
  count(y, name = "Frequency") |>
  mutate(Percentage = round(100 * Frequency / sum(Frequency), 2))

subscription_summary |>
  kable(caption = "Term deposit subscription frequencies")
```

```{r}
#| label: response-plot

subscription_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = y, y = Frequency, fill = y)) + 
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(Frequency, " (", Percentage, "%)")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Term Deposit Subscription Outcomes",
    x = "Subscribed to a term deposit?",
    y = "Number of customers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The subscription distribution helps us understand the relative frequency of `yes` and `no` outcomes. This is important when selecting an appropriate performance metric for the classifcation models in later sections.

## Next Steps

In the next stage, we will create a reproducible 70% training / 30% testing split and five-fold cross-validation folds. We will then specify and tune a classification tree and a random forest, compare their test-set performance, and refit the selected model to the full dataset for the API.
